title: Question bank storage: first grilling round
intro:
Before building the **question bank** we need to settle where questions live and how they are versioned.

Answer what you can; defer anything that needs another conversation, and use *Need more info* when the question itself is unclear.

questions.header: Where should questions be stored for the first release, given reads dominate and writes come from a handful of coordinators?
questions.body: Today every read goes straight to Firestore and every write goes through a Cloud Function. A second datastore means a second backup story.

options.label: Firestore, one document per question
options.description: Same rules, same backups, same client SDK. Queries by tag need composite indexes.

options.label: Firestore + prebuilt bundles
options.description: Firestore as source of truth, plus a nightly bundle per Disciplina for fast cold loads.

options.label: Cloud SQL (Postgres)
options.description: Full-text search and joins, at the price of a VPC connector and a second auth model.

options.label: JSON files in Cloud Storage
options.description: Cheapest, but no queries at all.

questions.rationale: It keeps **one** datastore, one rules file and one backup story. Bundles can be added later without a migration, so the cheaper option does not close any door.

questions.header: How should edits to a question that already appeared in an applied Prova be handled?

options.label: Immutable revisions
options.description: Every edit creates a new revision; Provas pin a revision id.

options.label: Edit in place + audit log
options.description: Simpler, but a past Prova would silently change.

options.label: Freeze once applied
options.description: Applied questions become read-only; edits require a copy.

questions.rationale: Past results must stay explainable: a student's report has to show the question exactly as it was asked.

questions.header: Which authoring features must exist on day one?

options.label: Free tags besides the Conteúdo taxonomy

questions.rationale: Physics questions are unusable without formulas and figures; attribution is needed before anything is published.
